claims.text: Applying a uniform tungsten-doped diamond-like carbon coating to high-entropy-alloy components will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate over a broad temperature range.
Untreated high-entropy-alloy surfaces used in harsh moving-component environments may exhibit roughness and exposure-induced oxidation.
The proposed intervention is physical-vapor deposition of a uniform W-DLC coating.
The coating is expected to remain effective from approximately -50°C to 400°C.
Effectiveness requires an environment free of aggressive corrosive contaminants.
A coating thickness greater than 500 nm is a minimum effective thickness for maintaining coating integrity.
The deposited coating consists of a nanoscale amorphous carbon matrix containing tungsten carbide clusters.
The amorphous-carbon and tungsten-carbide-cluster structure improves mechanical hardness.
The amorphous-carbon and tungsten-carbide-cluster structure improves thermal stability.
The DLC coating provides a low-shear interface.
The coating minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact.
Minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact reduces adhesion and friction.
Tungsten doping enhances the thermal stability of the carbon network.
Enhanced thermal stability mitigates oxidation or structural degradation at high temperatures.
Mitigating oxidation and structural degradation sustains the coating's lubricating properties at high temperatures.
Relative to untreated controls, coated samples will exhibit at least a 30% reduction in coefficient of friction across the specified temperature range.
Relative to untreated controls, coated samples will exhibit at least a 25% reduction in wear rate across the specified temperature range.
The predicted improvement will persist only while the coating remains intact without significant delamination or degradation.
The predicted improvement requires surface stresses and corrosive exposure to remain within the coating's design limits.
Long-term adhesion, cyclic durability, and coating-substrate interactions across extreme thermal cycles are uncertain because no direct supporting evidence was supplied.
